prerequisites: ELEMENTS OF MECHANICS APPLIED TO MACHINES.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the complex of phenomena related to the interaction between the surfaces of mechanical and biomechanical systems in relative motion, even in the presence of lubricants.
Understand contents on contact mechanics, friction phenomena, wear and lubrication mechanisms that involve kinematic couplings.

Understand biotribology (tribology applied to biological systems), with particular reference to in vitro and in silico methods for the characterization of the wear phenomena of human joint prostheses and to the phenomena of dental wear.
Principles of contact mechanics and analysis of Hertzian couplings.
Parameters and instruments for the characterization of the topography of surfaces.
Mechanisms and modeling of wear phenomena.
Properties of lubricants.
Lubrication mechanisms and design of hydrodynamically lubricated bearings.
Phenomena of natural synovial lubrication.
Kinematics and musculoskeletal dynamics principles.
Human joint prostheses (THR, TKR) and their tribological behavior.
Dental dentistry.
Ability to use the Hertzian theory for the definition of the stress state and the thermal regime in mechanical couplings.
Ability to analyze the topography of real surfaces.
Ability to define the lubrication mechanisms of tribosystems according to the operating parameters and the rheology of the lubricants.
Ability to model tribological phenomena in biomechanical systems.
Ability to design mechanical couplings optimized from the tribological point of view.
Ability to model complex lubrication phenomena.
Ability to interpret tribological phenomena with reference to biological systems.
Know how to identify the most appropriate methods for the design and/or verification of tribological couplings.
Know how to describe the objectives, procedure and results of the developed topics, in a clear and concise way with good language.
Be able to apply the knowledge acquired to contexts different from those presented during the course, and delve deeper into the topics covered using materials other than those proposed.

syllabus_topics: CLASSIFICATION AND CHEMICAL-PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF LUBRICANTS
EVALUATION OF THE STRESS STATE AND SURFACE TEMPERATURES IN TRIBOLOGICAL COUPLINGS.
SIZING OF LUBRICATED BEARINGS AND STABILITY ANALYSIS OF ROTORS
MULTIBODY MODELS AND SOFTWARE FOR MUSCULOSKELETAL DYNAMIC SIMULATIONS
IN-VITRO AND IN-SILICO EVALUATION OF PROSTHETIC WEAR PHENOMENA

assessment_methods.method: Group work discussion during oral exam

assessment_rules: The final evaluation is obtained as the average of the partial evaluations. A minimum assessment level (18/30) is attributed when the student has fragmented knowledge and limited ability to use it. The maximum level (30/30) is attributed when the student demonstrates complete and in-depth knowledge and remarkable ability to use methodologies and tools. Praise is awarded for significant mastery, remarkable language properties, and autonomous processing capacity in various contexts.
